profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a developer-tools company for an internal experimentation-platform integration of a research proposal on classifying C code comments as Useful or Not Useful. The existing proposal uses contextualized embeddings and compares models trained on the original 9,048 labeled code-comment pairs against runs that include 739 additional generated code-comment pairs with LLM-produced labels. The design under review is not about inventing the model from scratch; it is about whether the proposal is implementable in the company’s shared ML experimentation stack without creating avoidable rework. The agenda is to review how the augmented data is represented in the pipeline, what the baseline comparison means in the platform, what 'meeting platform standards' requires for this first integration, and how the generated labels will be sanity-checked before use. The expected outcome is a decision on whether the design can proceed this sprint with minor edits or whether it needs specific revisions in the design doc.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: NLP experimentation, text classification pipelines, embedding-based modeling for developer tools
members.background: Priya adapted an academic prototype on code-comment usefulness classification into the company’s internal experimentation framework and authored most of the current design proposal. She has several years of experience running offline ML experiments quickly and translating promising research workflows into internal product prototypes.
members.private_state: Priya wants approval with as little redesign as possible so implementation can begin this sprint. She is trying to preserve the paper-style workflow, avoid extra platform ceremony for the first version, and keep the integration lightweight enough that the team can show model lift quickly.
hidden_assumptions: When the proposal says the data is augmented, the 739 generated pairs can simply be appended to the training input used by the training job, while the original benchmark split remains untouched.
If a design meets the experimentation platform standards, that mainly means it runs reproducibly inside the sandboxed experiment jobs and writes metrics in the standard format.
Baseline refers to the strongest non-augmented result already established in the current experimental setup, which serves as the number the augmented approach must beat.
A sanity check on generated labels means sampling a modest subset of examples to verify that the pseudo-labels and formatting look reasonable before training.
For a first platform integration, dataset handling details can stay close to the current CSV-and-config workflow as long as reruns are possible from version-controlled code.

members.name: Daniel Cho
members.expertise: Experiment reproducibility, dataset versioning, model lifecycle infrastructure, internal ML governance
members.background: Daniel supports multiple ML teams adopting the company’s shared experimentation and model-management stack. His job is to ensure that research prototypes can be reproduced, compared over time, and later promoted without hidden assumptions baked into one-off scripts.
members.private_state: Daniel wants to prevent a design from being approved in a form that will later require retrofitting for lineage, artifact comparability, or platform conventions. He is trying to steer the proposal toward platform-safe defaults without forcing a full productionization discussion.
hidden_assumptions: When a proposal refers to augmented data in the platform, the added 739 pairs should exist as a separately versioned dataset artifact that is explicitly joined into the training pipeline rather than quietly appended inside a job script.

If a design meets the experimentation platform standards, that means it already uses the platform’s required dataset lineage, artifact registration, and logging hooks so that future comparisons are trustworthy.
Baseline means the canonical executable reference pipeline the platform will preserve for future regressions, not merely the best prior score in a table.
A sanity check on a batch this small usually means a quick full-batch review before the data is committed as a reusable dataset asset, even if the review itself is lightweight.
Any data used in recurring experiments should be representable as first-class platform artifacts rather than informal local preprocessing steps.

misalignment_points.topic: What 'using the augmented dataset' operationally means
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss running experiments with 'the augmented dataset' and say the setup should stay clean and reproducible.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the training job reads the usual training split plus an appended CSV containing the 739 generated code-comment pairs, with the benchmark split itself unchanged.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the 739 pairs are registered as a distinct versioned dataset artifact that the pipeline explicitly joins at training time, so the augmentation step is visible and replayable within platform metadata.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are advocating reproducibility, and neither sees their interpretation as controversial because 'using the augmented dataset' sounds like a settled implementation detail rather than a conceptual design choice.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to comparing the proposal against 'the baseline' before approval.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the best non-augmented result already reported in the current experiment set, i.e., the score the augmented approach must exceed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means a locked, rerunnable reference pipeline artifact that future experiments can always execute for regression comparisons, regardless of whether it is the strongest prior score.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Baseline is standard ML shorthand, and in a design review both participants can comfortably say 'the baseline' without realizing one is talking about a benchmark number while the other is talking about a durable executable reference.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to meet platform standards
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the design should 'meet the experimentation platform standards' for the first integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means the workflow runs inside the platform’s sandboxed jobs, emits the standard offline metrics, and produces model artifacts in the usual experiment format.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means the workflow also conforms to the platform’s expected dataset lineage, artifact registration, and prediction/log schema conventions so later comparisons and promotion paths are not compromised.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like neutral organizational shorthand rather than a negotiable criterion, so each imports the standards most familiar from their own function and assumes the other is using the same bar.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to do a 'sanity check' on the generated labels before using the 739 added pairs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means inspecting a random sample of roughly 50-100 generated code-comment pairs for obvious label noise, malformed comments, or prompt artifacts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Daniel means doing a lightweight but complete pass over all 739 pairs before the batch is treated as an approved reusable dataset asset.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both treat the sanity check as a lightweight safeguard rather than a formal review stage, the hidden disagreement is about the boundary of the check, not whether one exists, so surface agreement feels perfectly natural.
